title: The Stinsons
cn: 第 15 集 · 斯丁森一家
novel:
The gang [[discovered|discover]] that Barney had a secret. He had been [[pretending|pretend]] to have a wife and son for years — all to please his [[aging|age]] mother.

"You what?!" Ted [[exclaimed|exclaim]].

Barney [[explained|explain]] that he had [[hired|hire]] actors to play his family. His mother was [[fragile|fragile]], and he could not bear to [[disappoint|disappoint]] her.

"She thinks I'm a family man," Barney said [[quietly|quiet]]. "She thinks I'm normal."

The gang was [[stunned|stun]]. They watched Barney's fake wife, a woman named Margaret, and his fake son, a child actor named Tyler. The [[performance|performance]] was surprisingly [[convincing|convincing]].

Margaret was [[professional|professional]]. She held Barney's hand and called him "honey." Tyler called him "daddy." Barney looked almost [[comfortable|comfortable]] in the role.

Then Barney's real mother [[arrived|arrive]]. She was sweet but [[sharp|sharp]]. She noticed small [[details|detail]] that did not add up. Barney's lies were [[crumbling|crumble]].

"Who are these people?" his mother asked.

Barney [[panicked|panic]]. But before he could speak, Margaret [[stepped|step]] in. "We love him," she said. "He's a wonderful husband and father."

Barney's mother smiled. "I'm glad."

Later, Barney [[confessed|confess]] to Ted. "I just wanted her to be proud of me."

Ted put a hand on his shoulder. "She already is."

Whether that was true or not, Barney [[needed|need]] to believe it.

pretend.en: to act as if something is true when it is not

exclaim.en: to say something suddenly and loudly

hire.en: to pay someone to work for you

disappoint.en: to make someone sad by not meeting expectations

performance.en: the act of acting or doing something

convincing.en: making you believe it is real

professional.en: doing something as a paid job

step.en: to move to help or act

confess.en: to tell the truth about something
